results.title: #BREAKING | 🇩🇿 🇳🇪 — Algeria’s parliament unanimously approved forward deployment of military forces into Niger.
results.description:
#BREAKING | 🇩🇿 🇳🇪 — Algeria’s parliament unanimously approved forward deployment of military forces into Niger. 

This expands Algeria’s presence at Air Base 101 (Niamey International Airport), established after the August 29 attempted coup. Forces will deploy to key oil infrastructure and Madama Air Base (21.9554711, 13.6470986) in the northeast.

Algeria has softened its stance toward Mali and Burkina Faso while backing the Niamey junta, recently supplying military helicopters. This shift counters the growing influence of Saddam Haftar and eastern Libyan factions, whom Niamey accuses of supporting Tuareg separatists and the anti-junta Patriotic Liberation Front (FPL). Some junta members blame the FPL for the August 29 attacks.

The deployment positions Algerian forces near FPL operational areas and the Libyan border, specifically Fezzan, which is controlled by remnants of Haftar’s 128th Brigade.

results.title: Algeria should just join the AES Algiers’ shift is understood to be driven by the growing influence of Saddam Haftar and eastern Libyan fact
results.description:
Algeria should just join the AES 

Algiers’ shift is understood to be driven by the growing influence of Saddam Haftar and eastern Libyan factions, which Niamey accuses of supporting Tuareg separatists in northeast Niger as well as the anti-junta Patriotic Liberation Front, FPL. Certain sections of the Nigerien junta have accused the FPL of orchestrating the August 29 attacks.

Algeria has long opposed the Haftar warlords, and the deployment to Madama Air Base places Algerian forces directly on the doorstep of FPL areas of operation in northeastern Niger, while also positioning them close to the Libyan border, particularly Fezzan, a region controlled by the remnants of the infamous 128th Brigade of Haftar's Libyan National Army.

results.title: A jihadist turf war is becoming a regional war.
results.description:
A jihadist turf war is becoming a regional war.

IS-Sahel claims it killed 400+ JNIM fighters in Burkina Faso's Oudalan (unconfirmed). ACLED counts 320+ JNIM–IS battles and ~2,200 deaths since 2019.

Now the fighting has spread to Niger Republic.
